findings.message: Status becomes 'converged' and the run freezes the first time the noisy loss dips below 0.02. Constant-rate SGD hovers in a noise ball rather than converging, so with small batches the scene can stop on a lucky dip and hide the key SGD behaviour. Consider not stopping, or requiring the loss to stay low for several steps. Not sampled.
Description says eight contour lines; the bowl shows about ten or more.
No capture varied batch size, so its effect on path noise (the stochastic part of the request) is not sampled; learning rate 0.01 is also unsampled.

Path, ball and both arrows sit in a small patch near the centre; the 0.08-radius trail blurs 14 short steps into a jagged band, and the arrow labels need pointer lines to reach their arrows. Consider a thinner trail or tighter framing on the running path.

Assumption says a diverged ball is drawn 'at the top of the bowl', but the host holds it at the rim (z=-2) at its true height 1.8875, about 0.2 above the surface there, not at the top. Align the wording or the drawn height.

At learning rate 2 the ball leaves the bowl in one step, so the learner sees a single straight jump past the lowest point rather than growing swings; a rate near 1 would show growing swings better (not sampled).
Host clamp holds the ball at the rim; it sits slightly above the surface there.
